summary: Documented the verified ACE environment facts: worker-model routing (probe before delegating, free-only rule, route show vs crew discrepancy), the pinned-config-check pitfall caused by a stale global ace binary, and switched the release checklist to npm run ace -- config check.

commands.command: opencode run -m opencode/fledge-alpha-free "Reply with exactly: OK"
opencode run -m opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free "Reply with exactly: OK"
opencode run -m nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash "Reply with exactly: OK"

checksNotRun: No worker was spawned to prove that a route change is honoured on spawn; the model probe proves provider availability, not crew wiring.
No paid model and no Codex runtime were used, per the task constraints.
Nothing was published, deployed or committed.
decisions: The docs describe the procedure (list, probe, set) rather than naming a model as the project default, so the guidance does not rot when free model names change.
The observed crew-vs-route-show disagreement is documented as unverified rather than asserted as a rule, because a spawn was not observed after the route change.
Routes for governor, supervisor and all seven worker roles were set to the verified free NVIDIA DeepSeek route; this is local .ace runtime state, untracked by git, and reversible with ace route set.
risks: The verified free route is slow (about 150 s for a one-word reply), so parallel workers would be minutes per turn; the work in this session was executed by the supervisor instead of delegating.
The global ace binary at ~/.local/bin/ace is an older snapshot that fails config check on the committed proagents handoff provider; anyone using it will see a false INCOMPATIBLE_ADAPTER.
docs/agent-workflow.md#worker-models describes behaviour of the pinned ace-proagents 0.1.4 only.
recommendedNextAction: Spawn one worker on the NVIDIA DeepSeek route for a trivial task and record whether the spawn uses the route set in .ace, so the documented discrepancy can be resolved with evidence.
